seo.metaTitle: Wrongful Death Lawyer in Pleasanton, CA
seo.metaDescription: Lost a loved one in Pleasanton? Our team handles wrongful death claims for families in Alameda County at no upfront cost. Two-year deadline in California.

hero.subtitle: When a death in Pleasanton was caused by someone else's carelessness, the family left behind deserves clear answers and steady support. We help families in Alameda County pursue wrongful death claims, and you pay no fee unless we recover compensation for you.

about.title: Pleasanton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasanton is home to about 79,510 people, and in 2025 the city recorded 324 injury collisions, 447 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths. Three is a small number on paper. For the families involved, it is everything. Many of the city's crashes cluster along I-580 in both directions and on southbound I-680, with a noticeable rise on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters head home through the Tri-Valley. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal charges the Alameda County District Attorney may pursue. It exists so that a spouse or domestic partner, children, and in some cases other dependents or heirs can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death claims on a contingency basis — you pay no upfront legal fees.

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before anyone files paperwork.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency close much sooner. We move promptly to protect your options.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We handle wrongful death cases on contingency. You will not be asked to pay legal fees up front.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash on I-580 in Pleasanton is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed on separate tracks. A criminal case in Alameda County is brought by the prosecutor and focuses on punishment, not on your family's losses. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family controls, and it can move forward whether or not a conviction happens.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. Each family's situation is different, so we will look closely at your specific circumstances. No outcome can be promised in advance.

items.question: How do we get started, and what does it cost?
items.answer: You share a few details about what happened, and we review your claim. There is no cost to speak with us, and we handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless your family recovers compensation.
